This isn’t just an app — it’s everything I’ve learned, all in one space to make your life easier. Or if you’d rather try it first, it’s £4.99 a month and you can cancel anytime. It’s everything I wish I had when I was trying to figure out what to cook every day- all in one place. No stress, no overthinking… just really good food made easier. If you want me to take the pressure out of meal planning for you, this is it 🫶 👉 Comment “BITE CLUB” and I’ll send you the link Much Love, Jade x

Under 30 | Under £5 Greek Doner Kebab – Inspired by @mezemike Serves 4 | Ready in under 30 minutes The recipe comes well under £5 after only using 1/4 cucumber & onions but pricing is easier and more transparent this way, if you can grab a fresh lemon for around 30p extra, if takes it to a whole new level. Ingredients – Greek Spiced Doner Meat: 500 g pork mince – £2.25 1 onion – blended finely (95p for 3) 1 tbsp olive oil ½ tbsp garlic granules ½ tsp salt ½ tsp black pepper ½ tbsp paprika ½ tbsp dried oregano ½ tsp cinnamon 2 tbsp Greek or natural yoghurt 2 tbsp tomato purée Flatbreads: 120 g plain flour (1 cup) 2 tbsp olive oil 1 tsp flaky salt 120g natural yoghurt (1/2 cup) Roasted Veg: 1 red pepper – £0.67 1 onion – cut into wedges Oil, pinch salt and pepper Tzatziki: 200 ml natural yoghurt – £0.55 Juice of ½ lemon (or a tsp cider vinegar) 1 tbsp olive oil ¼ cucumber – seeds removed & finely diced – £0.89 15–20 fresh mint leaves OR 1 tsp dried mint Salt to taste Total shop: £5.31 Method – 1️⃣ Prep the Doner Meat: Add the pork mince to a bowl. Blend the onion until very finely chopped or pulped. Add to the mince along with all remaining doner ingredients. Mix really well until smooth and well combined. 2️⃣ Shape & Bake: Lay out two sheets of baking paper. Spread the meat very thinly into a rectangle. Roll up tightly like a sausage using the paper. Bake at 180°C (fan) for 30 minutes. 3️⃣ Roast the Veg: Cut the red pepper into sixths. Cut the onion into 6 wedges. Add to a tray, drizzle with oil, season. Roast alongside the doner for 25–30 minutes. 4️⃣ Flatbreads: Mix flour, yoghurt, olive oil, and salt into a dough. Knead briefly until smooth. Divide into 4 balls. Roll out thin and dry-fry in a hot pan 1–2 mins per side until cooked. 5️⃣ Finish the Doner: Unwrap the doner from baking paper. Place back on the tray, unrolled. Return to the oven to keep warm — edges will crisp slightly (delicious). 6️⃣ Tzatziki: Mix yoghurt, lemon juice, olive oil, cucumber, mint, and salt. Chill if time allows. 7️⃣ Serve: Fill warm flatbreads with crispy doner meat. Add roasted peppers & onions. Drizzle generously with tzatziki. Much Love, Jade x

🍝 MILLION DOLLAR SPAGHETTI → LEFTOVER LASAGNE 💷 1.60 per portion | 8 portions 📱 Comment APP and I’ll send you the link to this Lidl meal plan on Instagram. Facebook/TikTok? Link in bio. One ragu → two family meals. The spaghetti makes 4 portions, then the leftovers become a 4-portion lasagne. My version of- 🍝 MILLION DOLLAR SPAGHETTI Ragu * 1 tbsp oil * 3 red onions, chopped * 500g beef mince * 2 tsp garlic granules * 1 tbsp paprika * 1 tsp cumin * 1 tsp coriander * 2 tsp oregano * ¼ tsp cinnamon * 2 × 400g tins plum tomatoes * 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce * 400g tin brown lentils, drained * 2 beef stock cubes Cheese sauce * 75g butter * 60g plain flour * 750ml water * 300ml milk * 375g mature cheddar * 2 tsp mustard * 2 tsp Worcestershire sauce * ¾ tsp salt + pepper To finish * 250g spaghetti * 100g cheddar Cook the onions and mince. Add everything else for the ragu and simmer until thick. Make the cheese sauce by melting the butter, stirring in the flour, then gradually whisking in the water and milk. Stir through the cheese, mustard, Worcestershire sauce and seasoning. Cook the spaghetti. Layer spaghetti, ragu and cheese sauce, top with cheddar and bake at 180°C fan for 20–25 min. 🧀 LEFTOVER LASAGNE Layer the remaining ragu and cheese sauce with lasagne sheets. Top with cheese and bake at 180°C fan until golden and bubbling. Serves 4. That’s 8 portions from one shop, across two completely different meals. ❤️ All recipes from this Lidl £25 meal plan are in my app, plus 400+ more recipes, meal planning, favourites and smart shopping lists. Recipes are always free here — the app simply puts everything in one place. Much Love, Jade x

🍲 French Onion Soup with Cheesy Croutons All **10 recipes from my Lidl £25 series** are now in my app! ❤️ Comment APP and I’ll send you the link. You can save your favourite recipes, save the whole meal plan and use the Smart Shopping List to generate your shopping list for you. 🍲 French Onion Soup with Cheesy Croutons Serves 4 * 1kg brown onions, thinly sliced * 50g butter * 1 litre beef or vegetable stock * ½ tbsp Worcestershire sauce * 1 tsp dried thyme * 1 tbsp plain flour * Salt & black pepper * 4 hotdog rolls * 100g cheddar (traditionally Gruyère) * Olive oil Method 1. Melt the butter in a large saucepan. Add the onions with a pinch of salt. 2. Cook over a low heat for 45–60 minutes, stirring regularly, until deeply golden and caramelised. 3. Add the flour, fry for a minute then add thyme and black pepper, then pour in the stock and Worcestershire sauce. 4. Simmer for 15–20 minutes. 5. Slice the hotdog rolls into rounds. Place on a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Toast until golden and crisp. 6. Ladle the soup into ovenproof bowls and arrange the toasted bread rounds on top. 7. Sprinkle generously with grated cheddar and place under the grill until the cheese is melted, bubbling and golden. 8. Serve immediately. 💡 Tip: Don’t rush the onions! That slow caramelisation is what gives this soup its deep, sweet flavour. Much Love, Jade x

🥔 **CHEESY POTATO CAKES** 🧀 Golden and crispy on the outside, soft and cheesy in the middle — these are such a useful little recipe to have up your sleeve! These are part of my **£25 Lidl shop → 10 recipes** meal plan, where I take one budget-friendly shop and turn it into 10 family-friendly recipes. 📱 **Comment APP** and I’ll send you the link to all 10 recipes in the app, along with the full meal plan and shopping list. Perfect for breakfast, lunch, lunchboxes or a snack, and a brilliant way to use up leftover potatoes. You can also make extra potatoes specifically for these and freeze a batch for another day. **Makes 6 small or 12 large** **YOU’LL NEED** 500g potatoes, peeled and chopped 100g mature cheddar, grated 75g plain flour, plus extra for shaping 1 egg 2 tbsp butter (optional) 1 tsp dried herbs (optional) ½ tsp garlic granules (optional) Salt & black pepper A little oil or butter for cooking **METHOD** 🥔 Boil the potatoes in salted water until completely tender. Drain well and leave to steam dry for a couple of minutes. 🥔 Mash until smooth, then mix in the butter, cheese, flour, egg, herbs, garlic granules and seasoning. 🥔 Bring together into a soft dough, then lightly flour your surface and shape into a round about 2cm thick. 🥔 Cut into wedges or use a cutter to make individual potato cakes. 🥔 Fry in a little oil or butter for 3–4 minutes on each side, until golden and cooked through. **MAKE AHEAD** Keep in the fridge for up to 3 days. Or cool completely, freeze in a single layer and transfer to a freezer bag. Reheat straight from frozen in the air fryer or oven until piping hot throughout. Save this one for the next time you’ve got leftover potatoes! 🥔 Much Love, Jade x

Mini Roasted Butternut Squash, Potato, Caramelised Onion & Cheddar Pies Makes 12 mini pies Sweet roasted butternut squash, golden potatoes, caramelised onions and mature cheddar wrapped in homemade thyme pastry. Perfect for lunchboxes, winter lunches or batch cooking. Ingredients **Pastry** * 300g self-raising flour * 150g cold butter, cubed * 1 tsp dried thyme * Pinch of salt * Cold water to bring together Filling * ½ large butternut squash, peeled and thinly sliced * 500g potatoes, thinly sliced * 2 brown onions, sliced * 200g mature cheddar, grated * 1 tsp Dijon mustard * 2–3 tbsp milk * 1 tsp dried thyme * Salt, pepper & olive oil Method Roast the squash, potatoes and onions with olive oil, thyme, salt and pepper at 180°C fan for 35–40 minutes until soft and golden. Make the pastry by rubbing the butter into the flour, thyme and salt. Add cold water until a dough forms, then chill for 20 minutes. Mix the cheddar, Dijon mustard and milk together. Roll out the pastry and line a greased 12-hole muffin tin. Fill each pie with roasted vegetables and the cheesy mixture, then top with pastry lids. Bake at 180°C fan for 30–35 minutes until golden. Cool completely before freezing. Reheat until piping hot. If you made yesterday’s butternut squash soup, scroll back to see how we used the other half of the squash. Please give butternut squash a go if you haven’t already — it’s seasonal, delicious and such an affordable way to add flavour to your meals. Much love, Jade x

🍂 Creamy Curried Butternut Squash Soup with Cheese & Onion Flatbreads 🍂 ✨ On the app you’ll find: ✔️ 360+ easy family recipes ✔️ Budget-friendly meal ideas ✔️ Meal plans & shopping lists ✔️ Recipes to help you plan ahead Comment **APP** if you’d like to join 💚 This is one of my favourite ways to enjoy seasonal squash 🧡 Butternut squash is grown here in the UK, affordable, naturally sweet and when roasted properly it turns into the most delicious creamy soup. Serves 6 🥣 For the soup- ½ large butternut squash, peeled & chopped 2 carrots, chopped 3 red onions, sliced 2 tsp curry powder 100ml single cream 1 litre vegetable stock Olive oil, salt & pepper Roast the onions, squash and carrots with olive oil, salt and pepper at **180°C fan for 35–40 mins** until caramelised. Save a handful of the roasted onions for the flatbreads, then blend the remaining vegetables with the curry powder and hot stock until smooth. Stir through the cream and season. 🫓 Cheese & onion flatbreads- 250g self-raising flour ½ tsp salt 2 tbsp olive oil Approx 120ml warm water 100g mature cheddar, grated Roasted onions Mix flour, salt, oil and water into a soft dough. Rest for 10 mins, divide into 4, roll out, fill with cheese and onions, fold and cook in a dry frying pan for 2–3 mins each side. And if you’ve got mango chutney in the fridge… add it 🤌 The sweet, spicy chutney with the curried squash soup is honestly unreal. It’s giving the same comfort level as tomato soup and a cheese toastie, but with an autumn twist 🍂 Full recipe also saved on the app 💚 Much Love, Jade x

BAKED NDUJA SPAGHETTI 🍝 Recipe 👇🏼 COMMENT “APP” AND I’LL SEND YOU THE LINK TO MY RECIPE APP ❤️ If you’re on Facebook or TikTok, just head to the link in my bio and it’ll take you straight there. As I’ve said in the voiceover, all of my recipes are shared here on social media completely free ❤️ My app is simply a way to have them all in one place, with meal planning, shopping lists and loads more — and it costs around the price of a coffee a month. This is one-dish pasta bake with minimal prep and maximum flavour. The spaghetti cooks directly in the oven with smoky, spicy nduja, sweet red peppers, onions and garlic, creating a rich sauce with hardly any washing up. Ingredients 300g spaghetti 1 tbsp olive oil 1 red pepper, finely diced 2 red onions, finely diced 2 garlic cloves, finely chopped 120g nduja 1 tsp salt ½ tsp dried oregano 750ml chicken or vegetable stock Splash of cream at the end! (100ml) Method 1. Preheat the oven to 190°C fan. 2. Add the dry spaghetti to a large baking dish and toss with the olive oil. 3. Add the diced red pepper, red onions and garlic. 4. Add the nduja, salt and oregano, then pour over the stock. 5. Cover tightly with foil, making sure it is well sealed to keep the steam in. 6. Bake for 50 minutes, removing the foil carefully and stirring halfway through to help the spaghetti cook evenly. 7. Once cooked, give everything a really good stir until the nduja has melted into the stock and created a rich, spicy sauce. Serve straight from the dish. STORAGE Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat gently with a splash of water or stock if needed. Great Nduja and full meal plan from @lidlgb oven dish from @bm_stores and olive oil @filippoberio_uk ❤️ Much Love, Jade x

Affordable Slow Cooker Beef Stew 🍲 A proper cosy beef stew that makes a little beef go further. Green lentils add extra heartiness and help create a rich, thick gravy, while the slow cooker does all the hard work. Serves 4 Ingredients- * 400g diced beef * 2 tbsp plain flour * ½ tsp salt * ½ tsp black pepper * 1 tbsp oil, for browning * 1 large onion, diced * 3–4 carrots, chopped * 2 garlic cloves, finely chopped * 2 tbsp tomato purée * 1 tsp dried thyme * 2 bay leaves * 150g green lentils, rinsed * 1 large baking potato, peeled and chopped into chunks * 1,200ml beef stock, plus extra if needed Method- 1. Brown the beef Place the diced beef into a bowl and coat with the flour, salt and black pepper. Heat the oil in a large pan and brown the beef in batches. Remove and set aside. 2. Build the flavour Using the same pan, add the onion and carrots and cook for a few minutes until they begin to soften. Add the garlic, tomato purée and thyme and cook for another minute. 3. Slow cook Return the beef to the pan, then transfer everything to the slow cooker. Add the green lentils, bay leaves, chopped potato and beef stock. Stir well. **Important:** The lentils absorb a lot of liquid as they cook, so it's better’to have plenty of liquid than not enough. If you're cooking for longer than the timings below, or your slow cooker tends to cook quite hot, you may need to add extra stock or water during cooking. Slow cooker timings LOW: 7–8 hours HIGH: 4–5 hours The beef should be beautifully tender and the lentils should have helped create a rich, thick gravy. If the stew is thicker than you’d like, stir through a little extra hot stock or water before serving. Remove the bay leaves before serving. Budget tip Adding green lentils is a simple way to make a smaller amount of beef go further, creating a hearty family meal without needing loads of meat. Approximate cost: £6.00–£6.30 total using @tesco British lean diced beef! Around £1.50–£1.60 per portion Much Love, Jade x

🛒 £26 LIDL SHOP CHALLENGE | 10 RECIPES ❤️ How far can you stretch £25? Well £26.06 but I had to guesstimate a few loose items 👀 I took one Lidl shop and turned it into 10 family-friendly recipes — including cosy dinners, freezer-friendly lunches, homemade treats and a few clever ways to make your ingredients go further. 🍽️✨ ✨ Want all 10 recipes? Comment APP below and I’ll send you the link to my recipe app ❤️ I’ll also be posting all the recipes here over the coming days! This prep is all about making food easily and affordably from scratch whilst trying new things too! 👏🏻 Here’s what I made: 🍝 Baked Nduja Spaghetti – a rich, comforting family dinner that serves 4. 🥔 Cheesy Potato Cakes – crispy, cheesy and perfect for using up simple ingredients. Makes 6 large or 12 small. 🥣 Creamy Curried Butternut Squash Soup – cosy, warming and perfect for batch cooking. Serves 4. 🧀 Cheese & Onion Flatbreads – soft, cheesy homemade flatbreads. Makes 4. 🥧 Mini Roasted Butternut Squash, Potato, Caramelised Onion & Cheddar Pies – proper comfort food in mini form. Makes 12 cupcake-sized pies or 1 large family pie serving 6. 🧅 Traditional French Onion Soup with Cheesy Croutons – a simple, comforting classic. Serves 4. 🍝 Millionaire Spaghetti – a rich and indulgent twist on a family favourite. Serves 4. 🥧 Leftover Lasagne – turning the leftovers from the Millionaire Spaghetti into another family dinner. Serves 4. 🍪 Golden Flapjack Cookies – buttery, oaty and perfect with a cuppa. Makes 8. 🍑 Easy Plum Preserve – a simple homemade preserve made from the fruit in the shop. Makes 1 jar. One Lidl shop. £26.06. 10 recipes. ❤️ Which one would you make first? 👇

The £25 shop is back and this time is from Lidl 🛒❤️ I’ve challenged myself to turn one basket of affordable ingredients into 10 family-friendly recipes — showing how far you can really stretch a budget shop. Today I’m sharing exactly what I bought, including the price of every item, so you can shop along if you want to 👀 This shop came to £26.06 and over the next few weeks I’ll be sharing everything I made with it — from cosy family dinners to freezer-friendly ideas and ways to make simple ingredients go further ❤️ 🛒 Lidl £25-ish Shop — Full Shopping List 🥩 Meat & Dairy 500g Beef mince 10% — £4.69 Mature cheddar — £4.85 British unsalted butter — £1.99 (price cut applied) Italian ’Nduja — £2.99 (£1 price cut applied) Subtotal: £14.52 🥕 Fruit & Vegetables 2.5kg Potatoes — £1.65 Red pepper — £0.70 Carrots — £0.69 Hot dog rolls — £0.99 Butternut squash — £1.59 Onions — £0.95 Red onions — £0.95 Plums 500g — £1.29 (£0.40 price cut applied) Lemons — £0.89 Subtotal: £9.70 🥫 Cupboard Self-raising flour — £0.70 Brown lentils — £0.45 Spaghetti — £0.28 Plum tomatoes 2 × 400g — £0.86 Single cream — £1.09 Subtotal: £3.38 🛒 TOTAL: £26.06 ✅ All of these recipes will be available on my recipe app later this afternoon. Comment APP and I’ll send you the link ❤️ Or if you prefer to follow along here, I’ll be sharing every recipe over the coming weeks 🤌🏼 Come back tomorrow’s reel to see what I made 👀🍽️

🍎Apple Cinnamon Oat Bars Aldi £25 Shop Recipe Makes: 8 or 16 bars A cosy apple pie-inspired breakfast bar made with simple ingredients. Perfect for breakfast, lunchboxes or an easy snack. Recipe note: I remade these and added natural yoghurt to the mixture. The yoghurt helps to round out the flavour and gives the bars a slightly creamier, richer texture while keeping them soft and moist. Ingredients * 540g Aldi apple sauce (approximately 2 jars) * 200g natural yoghurt * 2 eggs * 75g soft brown sugar (or light brown sugar) * 300g rolled oats * 2½ tsp cinnamon * 1 tsp vanilla extract * 2 tsp baking powder * ¾ tsp salt Method 1. Preheat the oven to 180°C fan and line a 20cm square baking tin with baking paper. 2. In a large bowl, mix together the apple sauce, yoghurt, eggs, sugar and vanilla extract. 3. Add the oats, cinnamon, baking powder and salt, then stir until combined. 4. Spread the mixture into the lined tin and bake for 35–40 minutes until golden and set. 5. Allow to cool completely before slicing into 8- 16 bars. To serve: Serve with a spoonful of natural yoghurt, a drizzle of honey or maple syrup and an extra sprinkle of cinnamon for the ultimate apple pie breakfast. Store in the fridge for up to 5 days or freeze for easy breakfasts and snacks. Storage Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 5 days. For the best texture, allow them to come to room temperature for a few minutes before eating, or gently warm in the microwave if you prefer them slightly softer. These bars are also freezer friendly. Once completely cooled, slice into bars and freeze in a freezer-safe container or bag for up to 3 months. Freeze with pieces of baking paper between the bars so they don’t stick together. Defrost overnight in the fridge or for a couple of hours at room temperature before serving. Prep ahead tip: Make a batch at the weekend and you’ll have easy breakfasts or lunchbox snacks ready to grab throughout the week. Much Love, Jade x

🍲 French Onion Soup with Cheesy Croutons

Serves 4

* 1kg brown onions, thinly sliced
* 50g butter
* 1 litre beef or vegetable stock
* ½ tbsp Worcestershire sauce
* 1 tsp dried thyme
* 1 tbsp plain flour
* Salt & black pepper
* 4 hotdog rolls
* 100g cheddar (traditionally Gruyère)
* Olive oil

Method

1. Melt the butter in a large saucepan. Add the onions with a pinch of salt.
2. Cook over a low heat for 45–60 minutes, stirring regularly, until deeply golden and caramelised.
3. Add the flour, fry for a minute then add thyme and black pepper, then pour in the stock and Worcestershire sauce.
4. Simmer for 15–20 minutes.
5. Slice the hotdog rolls into rounds. Place on a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Toast until golden and crisp.
6. Ladle the soup into ovenproof bowls and arrange the toasted bread rounds on top.
7. Sprinkle generously with grated cheddar and place under the grill until the cheese is melted, bubbling and golden.
8. Serve immediately.

💡 Tip: Don’t rush the onions! That slow caramelisation is what gives this soup its deep, sweet flavour.

🥔 **CHEESY POTATO CAKES** 🧀

Golden and crispy on the outside, soft and cheesy in the middle — these are such a useful little recipe to have up your sleeve!

These are part of my **£25 Lidl shop → 10 recipes** meal plan, where I take one budget-friendly shop and turn it into 10 family-friendly recipes.

Perfect for breakfast, lunch, lunchboxes or a snack, and a brilliant way to use up leftover potatoes. You can also make extra potatoes specifically for these and freeze a batch for another day.

**Makes 6 small or 12 large**

**YOU’LL NEED**
500g potatoes, peeled and chopped
100g mature cheddar, grated
75g plain flour, plus extra for shaping
1 egg
2 tbsp butter (optional)
1 tsp dried herbs (optional)
½ tsp garlic granules (optional)
Salt & black pepper
A little oil or butter for cooking

**METHOD**
🥔 Boil the potatoes in salted water until completely tender. Drain well and leave to steam dry for a couple of minutes.

🥔 Mash until smooth, then mix in the butter, cheese, flour, egg, herbs, garlic granules and seasoning.

🥔 Bring together into a soft dough, then lightly flour your surface and shape into a round about 2cm thick.

🥔 Cut into wedges or use a cutter to make individual potato cakes.

🥔 Fry in a little oil or butter for 3–4 minutes on each side, until golden and cooked through.

**MAKE AHEAD**
Keep in the fridge for up to 3 days. Or cool completely, freeze in a single layer and transfer to a freezer bag. Reheat straight from frozen in the air fryer or oven until piping hot throughout.

Save this one for the next time you’ve got leftover potatoes! 🥔

Mini Roasted Butternut Squash, Potato, Caramelised Onion & Cheddar Pies

Makes 12 mini pies

Sweet roasted butternut squash, golden potatoes, caramelised onions and mature cheddar wrapped in homemade thyme pastry. Perfect for lunchboxes, winter lunches or batch cooking.

Ingredients

**Pastry**

* 300g self-raising flour
* 150g cold butter, cubed
* 1 tsp dried thyme
* Pinch of salt
* Cold water to bring together

Filling

* ½ large butternut squash, peeled and thinly sliced
* 500g potatoes, thinly sliced
* 2 brown onions, sliced
* 200g mature cheddar, grated
* 1 tsp Dijon mustard
* 2–3 tbsp milk
* 1 tsp dried thyme
* Salt, pepper & olive oil

Method

Roast the squash, potatoes and onions with olive oil, thyme, salt and pepper at 180°C fan for 35–40 minutes until soft and golden.

Make the pastry by rubbing the butter into the flour, thyme and salt. Add cold water until a dough forms, then chill for 20 minutes.

Mix the cheddar, Dijon mustard and milk together.

Roll out the pastry and line a greased 12-hole muffin tin. Fill each pie with roasted vegetables and the cheesy mixture, then top with pastry lids.

Bake at 180°C fan for 30–35 minutes until golden.

Cool completely before freezing. Reheat until piping hot.

If you made yesterday’s butternut squash soup, scroll back to see how we used the other half of the squash.

Please give butternut squash a go if you haven’t already — it’s seasonal, delicious and such an affordable way to add flavour to your meals.

This is one of my favourite ways to enjoy seasonal squash 🧡

Butternut squash is grown here in the UK, affordable, naturally sweet and when roasted properly it turns into the most delicious creamy soup.

Serves 6

🥣 For the soup-
½ large butternut squash, peeled & chopped
2 carrots, chopped
3 red onions, sliced
2 tsp curry powder
100ml single cream
1 litre vegetable stock
Olive oil, salt & pepper

Roast the onions, squash and carrots with olive oil, salt and pepper at **180°C fan for 35–40 mins** until caramelised.

Save a handful of the roasted onions for the flatbreads, then blend the remaining vegetables with the curry powder and hot stock until smooth. Stir through the cream and season.

🫓 Cheese & onion flatbreads-
250g self-raising flour
½ tsp salt
2 tbsp olive oil
Approx 120ml warm water
100g mature cheddar, grated
Roasted onions

Mix flour, salt, oil and water into a soft dough. Rest for 10 mins, divide into 4, roll out, fill with cheese and onions, fold and cook in a dry frying pan for 2–3 mins each side.

This is one-dish pasta bake with minimal prep and maximum flavour. The spaghetti cooks directly in the oven with smoky, spicy nduja, sweet red peppers, onions and garlic, creating a rich sauce with hardly any washing up.

Ingredients

300g spaghetti
1 tbsp olive oil
1 red pepper, finely diced
2 red onions, finely diced
2 garlic cloves, finely chopped
120g nduja
1 tsp salt
½ tsp dried oregano
750ml chicken or vegetable stock
Splash of cream at the end! (100ml)

Method

1. Preheat the oven to 190°C fan.

2. Add the dry spaghetti to a large baking dish and toss with the olive oil.

3. Add the diced red pepper, red onions and garlic.

4. Add the nduja, salt and oregano, then pour over the stock.

5. Cover tightly with foil, making sure it is well sealed to keep the steam in.

6. Bake for 50 minutes, removing the foil carefully and stirring halfway through to help the spaghetti cook evenly.

7. Once cooked, give everything a really good stir until the nduja has melted into the stock and created a rich, spicy sauce.

Serve straight from the dish.

STORAGE

Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat gently with a splash of water or stock if needed.

Affordable Slow Cooker Beef Stew 🍲 

A proper cosy beef stew that makes a little beef go further. Green lentils add extra heartiness and help create a rich, thick gravy, while the slow cooker does all the hard work.

Serves 4

Ingredients-

* 400g diced beef
* 2 tbsp plain flour
* ½ tsp salt
* ½ tsp black pepper
* 1 tbsp oil, for browning
* 1 large onion, diced
* 3–4 carrots, chopped
* 2 garlic cloves, finely chopped
* 2 tbsp tomato purée
* 1 tsp dried thyme
* 2 bay leaves
* 150g green lentils, rinsed
* 1 large baking potato, peeled and chopped into chunks
* 1,200ml beef stock, plus extra if needed

Method-

 1. Brown the beef

Place the diced beef into a bowl and coat with the flour, salt and black pepper.

Heat the oil in a large pan and brown the beef in batches. Remove and set aside.

 2. Build the flavour

Using the same pan, add the onion and carrots and cook for a few minutes until they begin to soften.

Add the garlic, tomato purée and thyme and cook for another minute.

 3. Slow cook

Return the beef to the pan, then transfer everything to the slow cooker.

Add the green lentils, bay leaves, chopped potato and beef stock. Stir well.

**Important:** The lentils absorb a lot of liquid as they cook, so it's better’to have plenty of liquid than not enough. If you're cooking for longer than the timings below, or your slow cooker tends to cook quite hot, you may need to add extra stock or water during cooking.

 Slow cooker timings

LOW: 7–8 hours
HIGH: 4–5 hours

The beef should be beautifully tender and the lentils should have helped create a rich, thick gravy.

If the stew is thicker than you’d like, stir through a little extra hot stock or water before serving.

Remove the bay leaves before serving.

Budget tip

Adding green lentils is a simple way to make a smaller amount of beef go further, creating a hearty family meal without needing loads of meat.

Approximate cost: £6.00–£6.30 total using @tesco British lean diced beef!

Around £1.50–£1.60 per portion

🍎Apple Cinnamon Oat Bars

Aldi £25 Shop Recipe

Makes: 8 or 16 bars

A cosy apple pie-inspired breakfast bar made with simple ingredients. Perfect for breakfast, lunchboxes or an easy snack.
Recipe note: I remade these and added natural yoghurt to the mixture. The yoghurt helps to round out the flavour and gives the bars a slightly creamier, richer texture while keeping them soft and moist.

Ingredients
* 540g Aldi apple sauce (approximately 2 jars)
* 200g natural yoghurt
* 2 eggs
* 75g soft brown sugar (or light brown sugar)
* 300g rolled oats
* 2½ tsp cinnamon
* 1 tsp vanilla extract
* 2 tsp baking powder
* ¾ tsp salt
Method
1. Preheat the oven to 180°C fan and line a 20cm square baking tin with baking paper.
2. In a large bowl, mix together the apple sauce, yoghurt, eggs, sugar and vanilla extract.
3. Add the oats, cinnamon, baking powder and salt, then stir until combined.
4. Spread the mixture into the lined tin and bake for 35–40 minutes until golden and set.
5. Allow to cool completely before slicing into 8- 16 bars.
To serve:
Serve with a spoonful of natural yoghurt, a drizzle of honey or maple syrup and an extra sprinkle of cinnamon for the ultimate apple pie breakfast.
Store in the fridge for up to 5 days or freeze for easy breakfasts and snacks.

Storage
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 5 days. For the best texture, allow them to come to room temperature for a few minutes before eating, or gently warm in the microwave if you prefer them slightly softer.
These bars are also freezer friendly. Once completely cooled, slice into bars and freeze in a freezer-safe container or bag for up to 3 months. Freeze with pieces of baking paper between the bars so they don’t stick together. Defrost overnight in the fridge or for a couple of hours at room temperature before serving.
Prep ahead tip: Make a batch at the weekend and you’ll have easy breakfasts or lunchbox snacks ready to grab throughout the week.

Jade x
